title: Maximum Number of Robots Within Budget
summary: Given n robots with individual charge and running costs, find the maximum number of consecutive robots that can be run within a specified budget, where the cost is the maximum charge time plus the running cost multiplied by the number of robots.
statement: Given n robots with individual charge and running costs, find the maximum number of consecutive robots that can be run within a specified budget, where the cost is the maximum charge time plus the running cost multiplied by the number of robots.
constraints: Both cost arrays have equal length from 1 through 50000.
A consecutive window of k robots costs max(charge_times)+k*sum(running_costs).
Return the greatest affordable window length; return zero when even one robot exceeds budget.
hints: Affordability is monotone when the left boundary moves right.
Maintain the running-cost sum and a decreasing deque of charge-time indices for the current window maximum.
Extend right, shrink left while max_charge+length*running_sum exceeds budget, and record the largest valid length.
Every window considered by the two pointers has an exact O(1) cost query; once a window is too expensive, extending it cannot restore affordability, so discarding its left endpoint is safe.

tests.explanation: The first three robots cost 6+3*(2+1+3)=24, while no length-four window fits.
Every individual charge plus running cost exceeds nineteen, so the answer is zero.
